title: [factory-setup-agent] Sandbox amended: commands.test wired up, but the runbook half of the report cannot be delivered by an amendment
body:
Amendment episode for report `9f1defd34b78058b`. The round's design is in the `setup-round-*` artifact; `.factory/bin/bsf sandbox check` passes on it (`valid sandbox manifest, tier renders`).

## What changed

`commands.test` is no longer `null`. It is now:

```
npm test --if-present
```

`capabilities.not_exercised` no longer claims "the repo has no test framework, no test files and no test script"; that entry is replaced with one about total coverage, which really is still unmeasurable until a suite merges.

## Deviation from the report's literal wording — please read this one

The report asked for `npm test`. I set `npm test --if-present` instead. Measured, not assumed:

| Where | `npm test` | `npm test --if-present` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default branch, after `npm ci` | **exit 1**, `Missing script: "test"` | exit 0, nothing run |
| PR #12's tree (the report's own) | 31 tests, exit 0 | 31 tests, exit 0 |
| PR #12 + a deliberately failing assertion | exit 1 | **exit 1** |
| Empty directory (the trial's control step) | exit 254 | exit 254 |

`factory-setup-trial.yml` uses `actions/checkout@v4` with no `ref`, so the trial measures the **default branch** — where PR #12 has not merged and there is no `test` script. `reachedTier` in the runner returns `static` the moment the test step fails, and the run and screenshot steps are guarded on every prior step being ok, so they would be skipped. Taking the wording literally would have measured `static`, frozen a worse sandbox than the one already in place, and still not run anyone's tests.

There is no third option. A command that passes on a tree with no `test` script cannot also fail on one. `--if-present` is the only wording that is correct on the default branch and on a PR branch at the same time.

The report's actual need is met: `bsf gates tests` runs `commands.test` verbatim through bash in the repo root against the PR's own head commit, where the script exists, so it gets the real run and fails on red. `bsf gates coverage` runs immediately after it in the same job and reads `coverage/lcov.info` from the root — which that run has just written. On #12 that file has one record per `src/` file with repo-relative paths (`SF:src/db.js`) and 98.04% total line coverage, matching the report exactly.

**Follow-up worth tracking:** once a `test` script is on the default branch, `--if-present` and plain `npm test` are the same command, and the flag then only hides a mistake — deleting the `test` script would pass the gate quietly. Dropping it is a one-line amendment. The cost in the meantime is recorded in `capabilities.not_exercised`: on a branch with no `test` script the tests gate now reports **success** rather than the **neutral** it reported when `commands.test` was `null`.

## The half of the report I could not deliver

The report also asks for the `## Test` section of `.factory/definition/context/runbook.md` ("This repo has no tests."). I rewrote it, along with the rows in `feature-map.md`, `fundamentals.md` and `history.md` that rest on the same premise, and they are in the round artifact under `context/`.

**They will not reach the repo.** `factory-setup.yml` copies the context only on a non-amendment round:

```bash
# An amendment changes the sandbox only; the context stays the
# user's once it has been merged.
if [ -z "$AMEND" ] && [ -d "$design/context" ]; then cp "$design/context/"*.md .factory/definition/context/; fi
```

`research-domains.txt` and `stubs/` are copied unconditionally; the four context files are not. So an amendment episode structurally cannot fix a context file, and `runbook.md` will keep saying "This repo has no tests" on the default branch until someone either applies the rewritten section by hand from the artifact or runs a full (non-amendment) setup round. That is a factory gap, not something I can work around from here.

## Two things found on the way that are worth someone's attention

**Five competing first test suites are open at once** — #11, #12, #13, #14, #15 — and none has merged. They disagree: #11 and #15 run plain `node --test` and emit no coverage report at all; #12 adds a `pretest` hook creating `coverage/`; #13 and #14 inline `mkdir -p coverage`; three use `tests/` and two use `test/`. All five agree on the runner (node's built-in `node --test`, no new dependency) and all five are run by `npm test`, which is why the manifest drives them through npm rather than naming a runner — it does not need another amendment when a different one merges. But **whether total coverage can ever be measured depends on which one lands**, since #11 and #15 write no `lcov.info`.

**An earlier amendment is already open and unmerged.** PR #19 answers a different report (`002d0ba19faa9525`) and reaches the identical conclusion from the identical measurements. Since it has not merged, this round started from the default branch's `commands.test: null` and carries the change itself; `amended_by` lists both keys, so whichever of the two PRs merges second supersedes the first with a complete record. Closing one of them would save a review.

## Everything else re-verified unchanged

`npm ci` (exit 0) → `node src/server.js` (`listening on 3000`) → all six routes by curl → the seed command (`/report`: lines 3, units 16, value $297.37) → Chromium via Playwright against ` (127.0.0.1/redacted) the Stock heading, the four-column table with a delete link per row,  `total: $297.37` , the three form fields and the export link; filling Bolt / 5 / 275 and clicking add took the total to $311.12 (qty × price); full-page screenshot taken; the only console entry is the expected 404 for  `/favicon.ico` . Still  `renders\`.

One control from round 1 I could not repeat: `npm ci` under `env -i` with only PATH/HOME/TMPDIR/LANG/CI/PORT fails here, because `env -i` also drops the proxy variables this runner's firewall needs to reach the registry. Plain `npm ci` was re-run and passed. Noted in the manifest rather than left as a silent inherited claim.

Guardrails were skipped, as the instructions require on an amendment.
